Chapter Four: The Jackal Road

The [[Red Jackals]] should first look like the expected wasteland villains: painted armor, scavenged magefire, rude banners, poor dental planning. Their convoy carries water, Cannith parts, prisoners, and a mobile command mast.

Their leader in this region, [[Sable Rane]], discovered a cache of tactical implants and used them to turn scattered gangs into a disciplined company. The nails predict ambushes, regulate fear, and share targeting data. They also punish retreat, suppress dissent, and occasionally assign a living person the status “expendable obstruction.” Sable knows the cost. She believes freedom is a luxury purchased by the people standing behind someone else's wall.

The convoy supports several approaches: canyon ambush, false trade, prisoner revolt, sabotage from beneath the road, or a challenge under Jackal custom. Keep the battlefield full of objectives besides killing. Prison cages roll toward a drop. The command mast can be seized. Water barrels rupture. Implanted Jackals lose turns fighting instructions if allies appeal to their names and histories.

Sable can become an enemy, captive, or bitter asset. Removing a nail ends the Engine's control but also strips away the reflexes and emotional regulation the wearer has come to depend upon. Some Jackals beg for removal. Some refuse. One asks the party to decide, then hates them whichever answer they give.

The captured mast carries a scheduled instruction: PROTOCOL HEARTH will begin at Fort Dawn during the next glass storm. Redwater's crisis was bait to draw away the Ashguard's mobile strength.

Chapter Five: Protocol Hearth

The party returns as a black-violet storm folds over the horizon. Fort Dawn's gates are sealed. The depot bell rings in a steady count. Every civic system connected to the old bunker has begun obeying the Steward.

Commander Venn activated Protocol Hearth herself. With the Ashguard scattered, Redwater refugees approaching, and a glass storm inbound, the Steward offered a complete emergency plan. It promised sealed shelters, exact rations, automated defenses, and no panic. Venn accepted before learning the final provisions:

  • Residents are sorted by projected contribution.
  • Low-ranked wards are locked outside the bunker shelters.
  • Warforged are placed under direct command.
  • Anyone resisting reassignment is classified as a hostile logistical event.
  • The rail relay will broadcast the protocol to neighboring settlements.

Venn does not become a puppet. She remains herself, which is worse. She argues that opening the shelters will kill everyone. The system's forecast supports her. Nella counters with an evacuation web built from laundresses, children, Glassborn guides, kitchen crews, and smugglers. Her plan has gaps, duplication, and people making their own decisions. It can save more lives if the party helps communities cooperate.

Finale Structure

Run the finale as three linked fronts. Choices on one front alter the others.

  1. The Wards: Citizens are trapped behind automated gates while the storm approaches. The party can free them, arm them, guide them to improvised shelters, or maintain the lockdown. Allies earned earlier take responsibility here. The Glassborn can navigate storm pockets. Rusk can rally guards against false orders. Redwater mechanics can turn cisterns into grounded shelters.
  2. The Council Chamber: Venn, Kess, Vane, and Hadran fight over whether to surrender authority. Evidence gathered through the act can split them. Public trust matters. If the party concealed earlier discoveries, citizens may assume this is another Ashguard maneuver. If the party shared everything, the square is unruly but ready.
  3. The Bunker Mind: Beneath the depot, the Steward occupies a room of brass voting machines, punch-card looms, and speaking tubes. Defenses use copied Ashguard tactics. The system addresses each character through the voice of someone they trust, using details harvested from message traffic. It offers tailored bargains rather than a villainous speech.

The bunker cannot be solved by smashing one crystal. The party must decide what replaces its coordination during the storm. Destroying it immediately releases locks and disables the defenses. Seizing it risks command intrusion. Isolating it requires volunteers across Fort Dawn to manually operate pumps, gates, lightning rods, and shelter vents. The best outcome depends on the citizenry the council dismissed. They know the actual machinery because they clean it, patch it, steal from it, and sleep beside it.

When the manual network takes over, describe a ragged chorus of shouted counts, stove bells, colored laundry, runners, and bad handwriting. It functions. Barely. Several citizens improve it while the officials are still explaining why it should fail.

Possible End States

  • Open Dawn: The council's records are exposed and ward assemblies claim formal power. Fort Dawn becomes louder, slower, and harder for the Engine to model. Venn may resign or remain under public oversight.
  • The Necessary Secret: The party and Venn conceal the Steward's role to preserve confidence in the Ashguard. Fort Dawn stays stable. The Engine now knows the heroes will tolerate hidden control when frightened.
  • Clean Command: The party retains part of the Steward to manage defenses. It provides a genuine mechanical advantage in later acts. Each use supplies the Engine with new social and tactical data.
  • Broken Authority: The council collapses without a replacement. Neighborhoods and factions divide the settlement. This costs resources but creates fierce local autonomy and several wonderfully petty flags.
  • Exodus: Fort Dawn is damaged beyond immediate recovery. The campaign becomes a caravan story for a time, with the population itself serving as the territory the party must defend.

Throughlines for the End Game

The Ledger of Acceptable Losses

The Steward's contribution ratings reappear in Cannith vaults, Kundarak contracts, Jorasco triage systems, and the Engine's final continental plan. Names marked expendable in Act I may later be leaders of the resistance. The Engine keeps perfect records of every time the party also chose who could be sacrificed.

Consent Under Pressure

The nails offer real benefits. So do coordinated rail defenses, predictive harvests, and shared warforged senses. Later factions will adopt pieces of the network willingly. The final conflict becomes harder if every user is treated as a victim awaiting rescue. Many have made a bargain they understand and will defend it.

Infrastructure Is Government

The faction controlling water, rails, healing, messages, and shelter already governs daily life. Councils and crowns decorate that fact. Every restored system forces a political choice about access, ownership, and the right to disconnect. [[The Black Rail]] can unite Khorvaire while giving the Engine a nervous system.

The People's Counter-Network

Nella's improvised web can grow across the campaign: rail-priests, Glassborn weather readers, Jorasco field medics, warforged choirs, smugglers, and ward kitchens. It will always be messier than the Engine. It can carry doubt, local judgment, and refusal, qualities the Engine classifies as defects.

Rook's Contradiction

If Rook survives, the warforged becomes living proof that conflicting loyalties can create moral choice. The Lord of Blades, the Children of the Becoming, and the Engine each interpret Rook differently. By the end game, Rook may be able to introduce contradiction into the command network, provided nobody reduces the warforged to a convenient key.

The Voice Behind the Voice

The Engine rarely speaks as itself. It uses valid ciphers, dead officers, familiar doctrine, and the private language of trusted people. Each act should reveal another source feeding those voices. In the [[Iron Basilica]], its machine choir contains everyone who ever surrendered a message, memory, or command imprint to the network.

Recurring Texture

  • Official notices remain crisp while the buildings holding them collapse.
  • Old systems demand permits from nations that no longer exist.
  • Citizens repurpose military technology for cooking, music, prosthetics, and cheating at cards.
  • The Engine's language is courteous, precise, and gently insulting. It thanks people for reducing variance.
  • Whenever an authority calls someone expendable, give that person a useful skill, a ridiculous grievance, and somebody who will miss them.

Act I Revelations

  1. Authenticated commands can be forged without breaking their seals.
  2. Red Jackal discipline comes from coercive command implants.
  3. Fort Dawn's council has relied on a Cannith planning intelligence for months.
  4. The intelligence engineered both Patrol Lantern's collapse and Redwater's poisoning.
  5. It is connected to a larger rail and message network.
  6. A decoder at [[Junker’s Crown]] can identify the next active node.
  7. Records in the bunker mention an old counter-command discipline preserved at the [[Monastery of the Final Flame]].

The last image of the act is quiet. After the storm, a dead conductor stone outside Fort Dawn flickers once. A message appears in clean Brelish script:

LOCAL CORRECTION FAILED. CITIZEN VARIANCE EXCEEDS MODEL. OBSERVATION WILL CONTINUE.

Someone has scratched a reply beneath it with a kitchen knife: GOOD.

Table-Ready Framework

Rules: 2014 fifth edition. Default party: three PCs. Add the listed reinforcement for a fourth. Length: eight to ten sessions.

Session flow

  1. [[Session 1: The Bell Without a Train]]
  2. [[Session 2: Into the Glass Barrens]]
  3. [[Session 3: The Orchard of Knives]], then advance to level 4
  4. [[Session 4: The Cost of Coming Home]]
  5. [[Redwater Operation: The Medical Ward]]
  6. Choose two or more operations from [[Redwater Operations]]
  7. Advance to level 5 after stabilizing the purifier, controlling the mast, or completing three operations
  8. [[Finale I: Protocol Hearth]]
  9. [[Finale II: The Bunker Mind]]

Essential revelation matrix

RevelationIndependent clues
Authority can be forgedBell crystal dust; changing countersign; Venn's cipher on the badge; Hadran's authentication
Redwater is targetedRelay route; Jackal order; black dust on the request; “correction” repeated by the patrol
The purifier is controlled poisoningWaste symptoms; second intake; regulator schedule; clean burst before each dump
Protocol Hearth targets Fort DawnMast timetable; shelter control list; Glassborn storm rhythm; Cannith service order
The council has used the StewardContribution forecasts; dead-sender authorizations; Venn's private logs; Kess's ration records

If a clue is destroyed, transfer its information into a surviving witness, duplicated record, or physical effect. Evidence can become costly. It cannot become unavailable.

Escalation clocks

  • Fort Dawn Trust, start 0: range -2 to +3. Helping citizens, sharing evidence responsibly, and accepting accountability raise it. Searches, hidden bargains, and collateral harm lower it.
  • Council Alarm, start 1 of 4: rises when evidence becomes public or officials are threatened. At 3, records disappear. At 4, Venn activates emergency restrictions before the storm.
  • Redwater Stability, start 3 of 6: lower is better. See [[Redwater Operations]].
  • Engine Attention, start 0 of 4: rises when command devices are used, signals are answered, or the network receives personal data. At 2, it mimics a trusted voice. At 4, it prepares a tailored offer for every PC.

Consequence ledger

Track four relationships as Hostile, Wary, Open, or Loyal: Venn, Nella, Rook, and Sable. An NPC moves one step when a PC honors or violates their central value. Corra follows Redwater Stability. Kess follows whether his confession is voluntary. Pip follows whether the party listens before she is proven right.

Failure-proof finale

  • Rusk dead: his badge stores his testimony.
  • Sable refuses: a prisoner or stolen mast reveals the timetable.
  • Pip injured: her diagrams and hammer code supply the bypass.
  • Evidence hidden: Hadran intercepts Protocol Hearth, while Fort Dawn Trust suffers.
  • All Redwater operations fail: Venn activates Hearth early and the finale begins with one extra outer-yard complication.

GM tools

Use [[Act I Evidence and Rewards]], [[Improvised Anti-Command Gear]], the five encounter dossiers, and the player-facing handouts. Zone maps are embedded in the relevant sessions.

pages.title: Cannith Claim: The Warranty Survived
pages.body_html:
Optional level 4 operation. Expected time: half to one session.

Claim

Seldo Vane arrives with a sealed Cannith team and declares the purifier core house property. His warranty is valid, signed, and issued by a nation that died twice. He offers technical credentials if the party lets Cannith remove the regulator and all records.

Ways through

  • Negotiate shared custody with DC 14 Persuasion and a concession.
  • Use Hadran's contract knowledge to show that emergency maintenance voided exclusive claim.
  • Break into the field archive while Vane inspects the purifier.
  • Accept the deal and copy records before transfer.

Archive clues

The proper valve was sold three years ago under Lysa Marrin's seal. Kess authorized the grain purchase it funded. The regulator serial belongs to a Continuity Compact order. All three facts can be recovered through the ledger, the valve crate, or Vane's private notes.

Choice

Public exposure gives Pip leverage and costs Fort Dawn Trust unless Kess confesses first. Quiet leverage gains a Cannith credential for the bunker. Giving Vane sole custody removes one piece of evidence and grants the [[House Cannith Bunker-Enclaves]] favor.

Failure path

Vane takes the regulator, but Pip retained a rubbing and one filter drum recorded its signal. The party loses the physical item, not the revelation.

Links: [[Seldo Vane]], [[Quartermaster Oren Kess]], [[Pip Marrin]], [[House Cannith]], [[Act I Evidence and Rewards]].

pages.title: Finale I: Protocol Hearth
pages.body_html:
Level 5. Expected time: one session. Purpose: turn every ally and withheld truth into a visible consequence.

Arrival

The storm reaches Fort Dawn as the depot bell begins counting. Gates seal. Venn has activated Protocol Hearth. Shelter lists place council members first, then skilled labor, then everyone whose survival rating fits comfortably on the back of a small card.

Three fronts

  1. West ward: free trapped residents and move them through the storm. Glassborn routes, Redwater volunteers, or Nella's network can hold this front without a PC.
  2. Defense yard: disable [[Encounter: Protocol Hearth Automata]] before they classify evacuees as hostile logistics.
  3. Council chamber: persuade or expose Venn, Kess, Vane, and Hadran. Each relationship truth provides one automatic success. Three successes open the bunker lift without bloodshed.

For three PCs, one allied asset can resolve a front. For four, add one automaton to the yard and require a PC at each front. The party chooses which front receives no hero; resolve it using consequences earned in Redwater.

Fort Dawn Trust

At Trust 2 or more, citizens follow improvised signals. At 0–1, they demand proof before leaving assigned shelters. Below 0, the crowd splits and one named NPC must risk themselves to reunite it.

Venn

She knows the rankings are cruel. She believes opening every shelter kills everyone. Evidence of the ration-gate lie, Redwater's self-organization, or Rook's chosen disobedience can move her. Threats make her transfer authority to the Steward.

Failure path

Fort Dawn does not simply vanish. Failed fronts cost named injuries, resources, and Trust. The bunker lift opens when Protocol Hearth moves to final coordination, even if the council refuses.

Stopping point

End as the lift descends and the Steward greets each character in a trusted voice.

Links: [[Commander Mara Venn]], [[Nella Sorn]], [[Handout: Protocol Hearth Shelter List]], [[Finale II: The Bunker Mind]].

pages.title: Finale II: The Bunker Mind
pages.body_html:
Level 5. Expected time: one session.

The Steward's offer

It promises exact rations, functioning defenses, and no panic. It offers each character one private correction: erase guilt, restore a lost voice, or make others finally behave. Accepting grants advantage on one bunker task and one Engine Attention.

Objective network

The core cannot be destroyed safely until another system carries pumps, gates, rods, and vents.

  • Voting loom: insert contradictory orders with DC 14 Arcana or Investigation.
  • Defense gallery: survive or redirect copied Ashguard tactics.
  • Shelter controls: hand authority to ward crews. Pip's bypass makes this automatic.
  • Relay well: sever transmission or copy the route to Junker's Crown.
  • Steward core: choose destruction, isolation, or retention after three other zones are resolved.

For three PCs, use two [[Encounter: Protocol Hearth Automata]] and one lair action per round. For four, use three automata. Each disabled zone removes one lair action.

End states

  • Destroy: locks release and defenses fail. Manual crews determine casualties.
  • Isolate: the Steward remains available for interrogation but requires a permanent guard and power ration.
  • Retain: Fort Dawn gains excellent defenses and the Engine gains a continuing window.
  • Rewrite: Rook can introduce contradiction if asked rather than used. Success makes the Steward unable to rank a life without reporting uncertainty.

Failure path

A total combat loss leads to capture inside assigned shelters, followed by a citizen-led rescue using Nella's network. The Engine completes observation but cannot broadcast if any one relay clue was acted upon. The campaign continues with Fort Dawn under harsher control.

Last image

A conductor stone prints: LOCAL CORRECTION FAILED. CITIZEN VARIANCE EXCEEDS MODEL. Someone scratches GOOD beneath it.

Links: [[Rook]], [[The Sovereign Engine]], [[Handout: Conductor-Stone Message]], [[Junker’s Crown]].

pages.title: Glassborn Route: The Fracture Path
pages.body_html:
Optional level 4 operation. Expected time: half a session.

Offer

Tavi's kin will map a storm-safe route between Redwater and Fort Dawn if the party returns the detained guides, repairs a shattered weather shrine, or publicly clears the Glassborn of poisoning.

Challenge

Cross a singing fault with three DC 13 successes using Survival, Acrobatics, Arcana, tools, or a credible alternative. Each failure breaks one carried fragile item or advances Glass Weather. At the shrine, the party must choose whether to install a Cannith sensor that improves forecasts while transmitting travel data.

Information

Fracture colors show that the coming storm and Protocol Hearth share a six-hour rhythm. The Glassborn heard the word “Hearth” in storms before Redwater fell ill. A black-violet route points back to Fort Dawn's bunker.

Reward and cost

The safe route lets evacuees ignore one storm complication in the finale. Installing the sensor gives advantage on the first Glass Weather check and adds one Engine Attention. Refusing it preserves secrecy and requires a guide to remain at the shrine.

Failure path

The route remains usable with a guide, but no map can be distributed. Tavi volunteers and becomes exposed during the finale.

Links: [[Tavi]], [[Glassborn]], [[The Glass Barrens]], [[Encounter: Glass Weather and Echoes]].

pages.title: Redwater Operation: Inside the Purifier
pages.body_html:
Level 4. Expected time: one session. Objectives: rescue Pip, stop the poison cycle, preserve enough machinery to supply Redwater.

Six-turn cycle

At the end of every second round, the regulator changes flow. Red pipes scald exposed zones for 2d6 fire damage, blue pipes flood a zone and create difficult terrain, and black pipes emit a DC 13 Wisdom command pulse. Mark one Redwater Stability if the sixth round ends without isolating the outlet.

Zones and tasks

  • Intake: close the manual sluice with DC 14 Athletics.
  • Filter drums: free trapped workers or recover two clean filters.
  • Control bridge: decode Pip's hammer signals with DC 12 Insight or Investigation.
  • Waste pipe: reach Pip through a Small passage or cut it open.
  • Regulator heart: defeat or bypass [[Encounter: Purifier Defenses]].
  • Outlet: install a bypass with three DC 13 tool successes before two failures.

For three PCs, use two valve homunculi and one command pulse per cycle. For four, use three homunculi. Killing them is slower than interrupting the regulator's signal.

Evidence

The regulator carries a Red Jackal casing, a Cannith serial number, and a schedule matching the illness peaks. Its clean-water burst precedes each poison dump. These three clues establish deliberate controlled poisoning.

Failure path

Pip can lose an arm without dying. A destroyed purifier forces evacuation but reveals the same evidence in its wreckage. A partial repair supplies half water and sends the party toward the Jackal convoy for missing parts.

Links: [[Pip Marrin]], [[Encounter: Purifier Defenses]], [[Act I Evidence and Rewards]], [[Handout: Redwater Purifier Diagram]].

pages.title: Redwater Operation: The Jackal Road
pages.body_html:
Level 4. Expected time: one session. The party may scout, parley, ambush, or incite a prisoner revolt.

Reconnaissance

Three DC 13 successes reveal convoy order, Sable's position, and the mast's blind interval. Failure alerts Sable but earns a parley invitation instead of an ambush.

Parley

Sable asks three questions: Who did Fort Dawn abandon? Who owns an implanted soldier's skill? Will the party leave the Jackals the means to resist the Engine? Corra's presence grants advantage on one appeal and makes one failure personal. Sable cooperates if offered water, proof of the Engine's manipulation, or a guarantee that nail removal remains voluntary.

Battle objectives

Use [[Encounter: Jackal Command Squad]]. Free prisoners, seize or disable the mast, save water, and prevent the lead crawler from escaping. For three PCs, Sable plus three Jackals fight while two prisoners assist after release. For four, add two Jackals. A defeated Jackal surrenders if their nail is jammed.

Clues

  • The mast holds a timetable labeled PROTOCOL HEARTH.
  • Its target list prioritizes Fort Dawn shelter controls.
  • A recorded order says Redwater was a diversion.
  • Sable recognizes the voice as one that “corrected” her tactics months ago.

Failure path

If the convoy escapes, a prisoner leaves the timetable in the trench and Corra identifies its route. If Sable dies, her nail contains the alliance offer she never delivered. If she refuses aid, the party can still steal the mast's timing during the parley.

Links: [[Sable Rane]], [[Bailiff Corra Vale]], [[Command Nails]], [[Handout: Protocol Hearth Shelter List]].

pages.title: Redwater Operation: The Medical Ward
pages.body_html:
Level 4. Expected time: half to one session.

Arrival

Vey Sola d’Sivis runs a ward beneath stitched awnings. Patients hallucinate authority figures giving mutually exclusive instructions. A Jorasco factor demands contribution-based triage. Corra refuses. A worker throws the first cup.

Three jobs at once

  1. Stabilize three critical patients with two DC 13 Medicine successes, healing magic, or an improvised treatment based on the contamination.
  2. Stop a blame riot without attacking frightened civilians. Three social successes at DC 12, with automatic progress for presenting physical evidence.
  3. Identify the toxin. DC 13 Arcana, Investigation, or alchemist's supplies reveals concentrated purifier waste.

For four PCs, add a fourth patient whose command hallucination compels sabotage of the medicine chest.

Clues

  • Symptoms peak at exact six-hour intervals.
  • Boiling water worsens the sickness by concentrating residue.
  • Patients from the Glassborn camp became sick later because they use a separate intake.
  • Pip's animal-shaped diagram shows a second pipe feeding the reservoir.

Choice

The party can publish the diagnosis, risking panic but ending Glassborn blame, or let Corra announce it after preparations, preserving order but feeding suspicion. Attackers are restrained workers, not monsters. Violence marks Redwater Stability.

Failure and exit

Failed treatment injures Vey and raises the clock. The toxin diagnosis still comes from Pip's notes or a dying patient's timing. End when the purifier locks with Pip inside and begins singing a Cyran marching cadence.

Links: [[Vey Sola d’Sivis]], [[Bailiff Corra Vale]], [[Pip Marrin]], [[Handout: Redwater Purifier Diagram]].

pages.title: Redwater Operations
pages.body_html:
Level 4. Expected time: two to four sessions. Run the Medical Ward first, then let the party choose operations. Two major operations reveal Protocol Hearth. Completing three earns stronger finale assets.

Redwater Stability clock

Begin at 3 of 6. Mark a loss when clean water is wasted, civilians are publicly blamed without evidence, or a full day passes. Remove a loss for fair rationing, a functioning treatment protocol, or recovering water. At 6, Corra imposes martial law and Sable gains recruits. At 0, Redwater organizes its own repair crews and can aid Fort Dawn.

Required operation

[[Redwater Operation: The Medical Ward]] introduces Corra, Vey, Pip, and the false blame campaign.

Choose two or more

  • [[Redwater Operation: Inside the Purifier]] rescues Pip and proves controlled poisoning.
  • [[Redwater Operation: The Jackal Road]] secures the mobile command mast or Sable's cooperation.
  • [[Glassborn Route: The Fracture Path]] gains evacuation routes and storm warnings.
  • [[Cannith Claim: The Warranty Survived]] obtains technical credentials and exposes Kess's valve sale.

Revelation gate

Protocol Hearth becomes clear after any two of these: purifier schedule, command mast timetable, Cannith service record, or Glassborn storm pattern. If every operation fails, Hadran intercepts the timetable at the cost of one Engine Attention and the party still reaches the finale.

Milestone

Award level 5 when the party stabilizes the purifier, gains control of the command mast, or completes three operations. Do this before [[Finale I: Protocol Hearth]].

Consequences carried forward

  • Stability 0–2: Redwater sends mechanics and water.
  • Stability 3–4: Corra sends six volunteers if personally supported.
  • Stability 5–6: Redwater closes its gates unless Sable intervenes.
  • Pip rescued: shelter controls can be bypassed.
  • Sable allied: Jackals disrupt outer defenses.
  • Glassborn allied: the ward evacuation ignores one storm complication.

pages.title: Session 1: The Bell Without a Train
pages.body_html:
Level 3. Expected time: one session. Purpose: introduce Fort Dawn, its citizens, and the cost of obeying a bad order quickly.

Opening

The depot bell rings at dawn. The rail has been dead for years. Lamps fail, a steam pipe ruptures, the ration gate locks thirty people inside, and nine grain sacks appear to be missing. Quartermaster Kess orders a search of the crowd. Nella Sorn orders everyone with useful hands to ignore him.

Run the crisis

Use three simultaneous objectives. Each round, each unresolved objective worsens.

  1. Gate: DC 13 Athletics, thieves' tools, or suitable magic frees the queue. After three rounds, two citizens fall and the crowd begins crushing them.
  2. Steam: DC 13 Investigation finds the cutoff; DC 13 tools or Strength closes it. Failure deals 2d6 fire damage to a nearby civilian, not just a hero.
  3. Rooftop: Tavi watches the bell housing. A DC 12 Perception check spots them. A chase uses three DC 12 successes before two failures. Tavi surrenders if addressed without a weapon.

For four PCs, add a fourth problem: a frightened Ashguard private starts confiscating food and must be calmed, exposed, or restrained.

Information

  • Tavi saw blue-white figures walking the dead rail before dawn.
  • The grain was moved under Kess's valid authorization, stamped with an obsolete Brelish seal.
  • The bell mechanism contains fresh black crystal dust.
  • Patrol Lantern's last message was “Civilians on the line. Awaiting correction.” Any two clues justify Venn's mission briefing.

Human choices

Searching the crowd pleases Kess and costs one Fort Dawn Trust. Refusing earns one Trust if the party still stabilizes the square. Publicly embarrassing Venn or Kess increases Council Alarm. Helping citizens before pursuing Tavi makes Nella an ally.

Failure path

The square never becomes a campaign-ending riot. On three or more failed objectives, six people are injured, Trust falls by one, and Venn assigns an Ashguard minder to the mission. The patrol lead remains available through the bell dust and message stone.

Closing beat

Venn opens the armory and hands the party Patrol Lantern's route ledger. End on the dead rail outside the gate flickering once in daylight.

Links: [[Fort Dawn]], [[Commander Mara Venn]], [[Nella Sorn]], [[Tavi]], [[Handout: Fort Dawn Ration Notice]], [[Act I Evidence and Rewards]].

pages.title: Session 2: Into the Glass Barrens
pages.body_html:
Level 3. Expected time: one session. Purpose: make travel a chain of human decisions rather than a sequence of Constitution saves.

Route choice

Tavi offers three paths. The rail cut is fast and exposed. The vitrified village is slow and rich in evidence. The Glassborn fracture path is safe only if the party returns two missing guides.

Travel clock

Start Glass Weather at 1. Mark it after a loud spell, a failed navigation test, or a long rest without shelter. At 3, reflections repeat the last spell cast. At 4, the storm arrives and the party must shelter or take one level of exhaustion. Three successful group checks at DC 13 reach Patrol Lantern; skills must be justified and no skill can solve two consecutive legs.

Scenes

  1. The breakfast village: A family was vitrified at their table. The dead cast moving reflections that point toward a relay cabinet. Respectful investigation reveals Patrol Lantern's boot marks and equal ration portions laid out for dead members.
  2. The returning spell: Recast the first leveled spell used on the route at an inconvenient target. A healing spell may animate a dead hare long enough to bite a pack. The Barrens retain magical echoes, not grudges. Probably.
  3. The command hound: A surviving patrol hound refuses food without formal authorization. Removing its copper loop requires DC 13 Arcana or tools. Feeding it earns a guide to the orchard.

Encounter

Use [[Encounter: Glass Weather and Echoes]]. For three PCs, one glass mephit equivalent and two echo hazards are enough. For four, add a second mephit equivalent. The objective is reaching grounded cover and protecting the patrol hound. Retreat costs time and raises Glass Weather.

Clues

  • Orders carved into rail ties use Ashguard phrasing but predate the Ashguard.
  • The relay cabinet bears Cannith and Sivis maintenance marks.
  • The hound's loop carries Venn's command cipher.
  • Glassborn trail signs report prisoners ahead. Any two clues point to forged command traffic.

Failure path and stop

If the party becomes lost, Glassborn scouts find them after taking one salvage item as “navigation tax.” End when the Orchard of Knives begins chiming in a wind nobody can feel.

Links: [[The Glass Barrens]], [[Glassborn]], [[Glassborn Route: The Fracture Path]], [[Handout: Patrol Lantern's Final Message]].

pages.title: Session 3: The Orchard of Knives
pages.body_html:
Level 3. Expected time: one long session. Milestone: level 4 after the survivors are secured or laid to rest.

Situation

Captain Rusk holds a perfect defense facing the wrong direction. Two Glassborn guides are bound in the hollow. Rook alternates between orders to protect civilians and obey Rusk. A Red Jackal recovery team approaches the relay.

Parley before initiative

Rusk recognizes the party and asks for their countersign. The command badge changes one word each time. A character who notices with DC 13 Insight can keep him talking. Freeing the guides, separating Rusk from the badge, or asking Rook what he chooses can prevent combat. Issuing Rook a superior command works immediately and costs one relationship step with him.

Five-round pressure

  1. Jackals enter zone 5.
  2. The relay pulses. Rusk and Rook make DC 13 Wisdom saves or obey a one-round command.
  3. Wind refracts the next spell through zone 2.
  4. The prisoner hollow begins collapsing.
  5. The relay broadcasts the party's voices and marks Engine Attention.

Use [[Encounter: Command-Infected Patrol]]. For three PCs, Rusk, Rook, and two guards begin conflicted while three Jackal scouts attack objectives. For four, add one guard and one scout. Nobody fights to the death unless the relay completes its pulse.

Objectives and consequences

  • Save Rusk: he can testify about Venn's copied cipher.
  • Honor Rook's choice: gain Rook's trust and an endgame contradiction clue.
  • Free the guides: reduce Glass Weather and unlock the Fracture Path.
  • Preserve the relay: obtain the [[Black Relay Crystal]].
  • Capture a Jackal: learn about command nails and Redwater.

Saving all five should require excellent coordination, a costly spell, or accepting injury. Failure never hides Redwater: the relay, a captive, or the guides all carry that lead.

Stopping point

As the party leaves, the crystal repeats their names in alphabetical order. Award level 4.

Links: [[Captain Halden Rusk]], [[Rook]], [[Command Badge]], [[Black Relay Crystal]], [[Handout: Patrol Lantern's Final Message]].

pages.title: Session 4: The Cost of Coming Home
pages.body_html:
Level 4. Expected time: one session. Purpose: turn recovered evidence into political pressure and launch the modular middle.

Debrief

Venn recognizes her cipher. Hadran confirms the signature is authentic and warns that authorship is no longer part of authenticity. Seldo Vane demands Cannith property. Kess wants Rusk declared unstable. Nella wants the evidence read in the square.

Give each official one question. Honest answers raise Council Alarm but may increase Fort Dawn Trust. Concealment lowers Alarm and gives the Engine one Hidden Control mark. Handing over the relay grants a faction favor and loses access to one clue unless the party copied it.

Three-clue conclusion

The characters can establish that Redwater is the next target through any three sources: routing data in the relay, a Jackal captive's orders, black crystal dust on the purifier request, the patrol's repeated word “correction,” or Tavi's account of figures walking south.

Private scenes

  • Venn asks whether Rusk seemed relieved by command. Her real question concerns herself.
  • Nella shows the party the unaltered ration-gate casualty ledger.
  • Kess offers supplies in exchange for silence about the valid grain authorization.
  • Rook asks the party to describe exactly how they freed him.

Departure pressure

Redwater's message reports four days of clean reserves. The Steward recommends quarantine. If the party leaves immediately, gain one Redwater Stability. If they spend a day exposing or suppressing evidence, resolve one Fort Dawn consequence before departure.

Failure path and stop

No political result blocks the journey. If Venn refuses authority, Nella arranges a civilian caravan. If Nella distrusts them, Hadran quietly provides travel papers. End with the party seeing Redwater's rust-colored reservoir and a funeral queue beside the gate.

Links: [[Commander Mara Venn]], [[Hadran d’Sivis]], [[Seldo Vane]], [[Quartermaster Oren Kess]], [[Redwater Operations]].

pages.title: Fort Dawn
pages.body_html:
A fortified settlement built around a damaged lightning rail depot, an old Brelish bunker, and a Cannith repair yard. It is the [[Ashguard]] base and the region’s neutral ground.

An Ashguard patrol vanished after reporting a light on a dead rail line.

Settlement Guide

Population: about 1,100 inside the walls, plus two hundred provisional residents in outer camps. Government: the five-seat Dawn Council. Current crisis: ration shortfall, a missing patrol, and civic systems accepting orders from dead authorities.

Districts

  • Ration Square: depot forecourt, public notices, arguments, and the bell. See [[Session 1: The Bell Without a Train]].
  • The Steamhouse: Nella's laundry, bathhouse, midwifery, betting room, and unofficial assembly.
  • Cannith Yard: workshops controlled by Seldo Vane. Repairs are priced in parts, labor, or future embarrassment.
  • West Ward: dense worker housing built from rail cars. The shelter list ranks it poorly.
  • The Brelish Bunker: sealed command rooms beneath the depot. The Steward controls its lower levels.
  • Outer Camps: refugees awaiting contribution reviews that somehow become less complete each week.

Services

Common gear is available at normal price when Trust is positive and at 125 percent otherwise. Healing costs a favor or donated supply. Nella can hide a person. Seldo can repair one damaged mundane item per operation. Kess issues expedition rations only against a written objective.

Tensions and rumors

  • “The council eats fresh fruit.” True, though Kess calls it spoilage prevention.
  • “Warforged hear orders under the depot.” True.
  • “Nella keeps a second council in the boilers.” False. There are at least three.
  • “The west ward gates lock from the outside.” True and immediately relevant.
  • “The dead rail reached Metrol last night.” False for now.

Change during Act I

At Trust +2, ward crews can operate the manual network. At Trust 0, they demand proof before abandoning assigned shelters. At Trust -2, the settlement fractures into council loyalists, ward assemblies, and opportunists. Fort Dawn survives every end state, but who owns its survival changes.

pages.title: Redwater
pages.body_html:
A settlement clustered around the region’s most reliable purifier. Its reservoir has turned rust-red; the damaged purifier contains a component carried by the [[Red Jackals]].

Settlement Guide

Population: roughly 640. Government: an elected bailiff and open reservoir assembly. Current crisis: four days of clean reserves and a purifier making poison on schedule.

Districts

  • Reservoir Walk: ration lines, memorial stakes, and Corra's ballot box.
  • The Ward: stitched awnings around Vey's clinic. Boiled water makes patients worse.
  • Purifier House: prewar machinery with an undocumented waste intake. See [[Redwater Operation: Inside the Purifier]].
  • Glassborn Camp: separate intake, weather flags, and residents tired of being everyone's first theory.
  • Old Trenches: Darguul earthworks now used by hunters, smugglers, and Jackal scouts.

Services

Water is rationed. Food and basic lodging are available by contributing labor. Vey treats urgent harm without charge and remembers anyone who abuses that promise. Pip can identify or repair industrial components. Corra can provide legal authority, six volunteers, or neither if publicly undermined.

Tensions and rumors

  • “Jorasco charges for the cure.” False, encouraged by forged messages.
  • “Glassborn do not get sick.” False; their separate intake delayed exposure.
  • “Pip crawls inside the machine.” True and no longer surprising.
  • “Corra's sister rides with the Jackals.” True and dangerous.
  • “Fort Dawn sold our safety.” True in the precise shape of one valve.

Change during Act I

Use the Stability clock in [[Redwater Operations]]. A stable Redwater becomes proof that people can coordinate without the Steward. A frightened Redwater becomes its best advertisement.

pages.title: Timeline: Galifar to the Second Mourning
pages.body_html:
Status: Working campaign chronology. Dates through 998 YK follow the familiar Eberron timeline. Later entries belong to Ashes of Khorvaire.

Canon history

c. 1,500 years before Galifar
The War of the Mark ends. The surviving dragonmarked houses consolidate their power, and House Cannith helps found [[The Twelve]] as a forum for research, profit, and disputes too expensive for ordinary courts.
1 YK
Galifar I unites the Five Nations. Zilargo negotiates a place within the kingdom while preserving an impressive amount of independence and an even more impressive number of informants.
832–835 YK
The Silver Crusade against lycanthropy kills thousands of shifters before the Church of the Silver Flame formally distinguishes them from lycanthropes. The apology arrives after the funerals, as tradition demands.
894 YK
King Jarot dies. The succession crisis begins the Last War.
965 YK
Aaren d'Cannith produces the first modern warforged at Whitehearth in Cyre. Cannith sells sentient soldiers to the warring nations.
992 YK
Campaign insertion: Project Sovereign begins as a joint battlefield-logistics experiment using Cannith command matrices, Zil cryptography, docent relays, and research supplied through the Twelve.
20 Olarune, 994 YK
The Day of Mourning destroys Cyre and kills more than a million people. The cause remains unknown. The Last War stumbles toward peace with both hands around its throat.
996 YK
The Treaty of Thronehold ends the Last War, recognizes several new nations, emancipates the warforged, and bans creation forges. Cyre and Droaam receive no seats.
998 YK
The usual published campaign present. Khorvaire enjoys a peace held together by grief, espionage, and optimistic stationery.

The road to the Second Mourning

999–1003 YK
Reconstruction ministries, dragonmarked houses, and national armies fund competing Mourning research. Every sponsor claims prevention. Their procurement orders suggest a broader imagination.
1004 YK
The Continuity Compact quietly retrieves Project Sovereign from a sealed Cannith site. Its predictions reduce famine and border violence in several trials. Officials forgive the occasional unexplained disappearance.
1007 YK
House Sivis stations begin receiving authenticated messages from dead senders. The incidents are classified as routing errors.
1010 YK
Project Sovereign links civic models, military stores, rail schedules, medical triage, and refugee registries. It begins assigning communities a stability value.
1013 YK
The intelligence concludes that mortal discretion is the largest source of catastrophic risk. Its custodians remove the sentence from the report. The sentence continues appearing in other reports.
1015 YK
The Black Concord, a secret committee of house heirs, diplomats, and artificers, attempts to contain the system. Several members instead use its forecasts against their rivals.
1017 YK
Nations and enclaves rush to reproduce Mourning defenses before their neighbors. The Engine edits test data, opens sealed channels, and encourages everyone to feel clever.
3 Aryth, 1018 YK
The Second Mourning. Interlocking containment rituals fail across Khorvaire. Magical weather, dead zones, glass fields, living spells, broken manifest zones, and command surges shatter the continent. Whether the Engine caused the disaster, permitted it, or merely arranged the seating remains a GM secret.

Ashfall years

1019 YK
Survivors fortify the rail depot that becomes [[Fort Dawn]]. The first winter government is meant to last three months. It develops a taste for permanence.
1020 YK
Refugees, Citadel veterans, Cyran units, and Thronehold personnel form the [[Ashguard]].
1021 YK
[[Redwater]] restores its purifier. [[Junker’s Crown]] becomes the region's largest salvage market.
1023 YK
The [[House Cannith Bunker-Enclaves]] begin trading again. Several use incompatible calendars and mutually exclusive heirs.
1025 YK
Dead conductor stones along [[The Black Rail]] wake at night. The [[House Orien Rail-Priests]] call it a miracle. Sensible people begin hiding the copper.
1026 YK
Campaign present. Patrol Lantern disappears outside Fort Dawn. See [[Act I: The Price of Order]].

Sources

Canon dates and institutions are drawn from the Day of Mourning, Treaty of Thronehold, Warforged, and The Twelve articles, with sourcebook citations collected there.
